1.1:
א,𐤀 How alone she sits, 
The city once great with people! 
Like a widow she has become, 
One great among the nations! 
A princess among provinces has become a slave!
1.2:
ב,𐤁 She weeps bitterly at night, 
And her tears are upon her cheeks.
Among all her lovers there is no comforter for her.
All her friends have betrayed her, 
They have become her enemies.
1.3:
ג,𐤂 Yahuḏah has gone into exile,
Because of affliction and because of harsh labor.
She has dwelt among gentiles, 
She has found no rest. 
All her pursuers have overtaken her
Between narrow places.
1.4:
ד,𐤃 The ways to Tsiyon mourn 
For no one comes to the Appointed Times. 
All her gates are deserted, 
Her kohenim sigh, her maidens are afflicted, 
And she has bitterness.
1.5:
ה,𐤄 Her adversaries have become chief, 
Her enemies have become at ease. 
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has afflicted her
Because of her many transgressions. 
Her children have gone into captivity before the enemy.
1.6:
ו,𐤅 And all the splendor has departed
From the daughter of Tsiyon. 
Her rulers have become like a buck,
They have found no pasture,
And they go powerless before the pursuer.
1.7:
ז,𐤆 In the days of her affliction and wandering,
Yerushalayim remembered all her pleasantries
She had in the days of old.
When her people fell into the hand of the enemy,
With no one to help her,
The adversaries saw her,
They mocked at her destruction.
1.8:
ח,𐤇 Yerushalayim has sinned greatly,
Therefore she has become defiled.
All who esteemed her despised her
Because they have seen her nakedness.
She herself has sighed and turned away.
1.9:
ט,𐤈 Her uncleanness is in her skirts.
She did not keep in mind her latter end,
And has gone down appallingly,
There was no one to comfort her.
“See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, my affliction,
For the enemy has made himself great!”
1.10:
י,𐤉 The adversary has spread his hand
Over all her pleasantries;
Indeed, she has seen:
The gentiles have entered her Miqdash,
Those whom You commanded not to enter Your assembly.
1.11:
כ,𐤊 All her people are sighing, seeking bread. 
They have given their pleasantries 
For food, to bring back life. 
“See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and look, 
For I have become despised.”
1.12:
ל,𐤋 “Is it naught to you,
All you who pass by?
Look and see if there is any pain like my pain,
Which has been brought on me,
Which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has inflicted on me
In the day of His burning displeasure.
1.14:
נ,𐤍 “The yoke of my transgressions 
Has been bound by His hand, 
Woven together and thrust upon my neck. 
He has made my strength stumble, 
Aḏonai has given me into hands 
Which I am unable to withstand.
1.15:
ס,𐤎 “Aḏonai has trodden down all my strong men in my midst,
He has called an appointed time 
Against me to crush my young men.
Aḏonai has trodden down as in a winepress
The maiden daughter of Yahuḏah.
1.16:
ע,𐤏 “This is why I weep.
My eye, my eye is running down with water,
Because the comforter,
Who could bring back my life,
Has been far from me.
My children are stunned,
For the enemy has prevailed.”
1.17:
פ,𐤐 Tsiyon spreads out her hands,
There is no comforter for her.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded concerning Ya’aqoḇ,
His neighbors are his adversaries.
Yerushalayim has become an uncleanness among them.
1.18:
צ,𐤑 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is righteous, for I rebelled against His mouth.
Hear now, all peoples, and see my pain. 
My maidens and my young men have gone into captivity.
1.19:
ק,𐤒 I called for my lovers, but they deceived me.
My kohenim and my elders breathed their last in the city,
While they sought food to bring back their life.
1.20:
ר,𐤓 “See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that l am in distress.
My inward parts are boiling up,
My heart is overturned within me,
For I have been very rebellious.
From without the sword has bereaved,
At home it is like death.
1.21:
ש,𐤔 “They have heard that I sighed,
With no one to comfort me.
All my enemies have heard of my calamity,
They have rejoiced that You have done it.
You shall bring on the day that You have announced,
So let them become like me.
1.22:
ת,𐤕 “Let all their evil come before You,
And do to them as You have done to me 
For all my transgressions. 
For my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.”

2.1:
א,𐤀 How Aḏonai in His displeasure
Has covered the daughter of Tsiyon with a cloud!
He has cast down from the shamayim to the earth
The comeliness of Yisra’ĕl,
And has not remembered His footstool in the day of His displeasure.
2.2:
ב,𐤁 Aḏonai has swallowed up, without compassion,
All the pastures of Ya’aqoḇ.
In His wrath He has thrown down
The strongholds of the daughter of Yahuḏah.
He has brought them down to the ground.
He has profaned the reign and its rulers.
2.3:
ג,𐤂 In the heat of displeasure 
He has cut off every horn of Yisra’ĕl.
He has withdrawn His right hand from before the enemy.
And He burns against Ya’aqoḇ
Like a flaming fire, consuming all around.
2.4:
ד,𐤃 He has bent His bow like an enemy.
He has appointed His right hand as an adversary.
And He slays all who delighted the eye.
In the tent of the daughter of Tsiyon,
He has poured out His wrath like fire.
2.5:
ה,𐤄 Aḏonai has been like an enemy.
He has swallowed up Yisra’ĕl,
He has swallowed up all her palaces,
He has destroyed her strongholds.
And He increases mourning and lamentation
In the daughter of Yahuḏah.
2.6:
ו,𐤅 He has demolished His booth like a garden,
He has destroyed His place of meeting.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has made the Appointed Times and Shabbathoth
To be forgotten in Tsiyon,
And despises meleḵ and kohĕn 
In His raging displeasure.
2.7:
ז,𐤆 Aḏonai has cast off His altar,
He has rejected His Miqdash,
He has delivered the walls of her palaces 
Into the hand of the enemy.
They have made a noise in the House of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄
As on the day of an Appointed Time.
2.8:
ח,𐤇 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has planned to destroy
The wall of the daughter of Tsiyon.
He has stretched out a line.
He has not turned back His hand from destroying.
And He has made the rampart and wall to lament;
Together they have languished.
2.9:
ט,𐤈 Her gates have sunk into the ground. 
He has destroyed and broken her bars. 
Her meleḵ and her rulers are among the gentiles.
The Torah is no more,
And her neḇi’im have found no vision from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
2.10:
י,𐤉 The elders of the daughter of Tsiyon 
Sit on the ground, are silent. 
They have thrown dust on their heads, 
They have girded themselves with sackcloth. 
The maidens of Yerushalayim 
Have let their heads hang to the ground.
2.11:
כ,𐤊 My eyes are spent with tears,
My inward parts ferment,
My bile has been poured on the ground
Because of the destruction of the daughter of my people,
As children and the infants languish
In the streets of the city.
2.12:
ל,𐤋 They say to their mothers, 
“Where is grain and wine?” 
As they languish like the wounded 
In the streets of the city, 
As their life is poured out in their mothers’ bosom.
2.13:
מ,𐤌 How shall I admonish you, 
To what shall I compare you, 
O daughter of Yerushalayim? 
To what shall I liken you to comfort you, 
O maiden daughter of Tsiyon? 
For your breach is as great as the sea. 
Who shall heal you?
2.14:
נ,𐤍 Your neḇi’im have seen 
Falsehood and folly for you, 
And have not shown you your wickedness, 
To turn back your captivity. 
But their visions for you 
Are false and misleading messages.
2.15:
ס,𐤎 All who pass by have clapped their hands at you. 
They have whistled, 
And they shake their heads 
At the daughter of Yerushalayim, 
“Is this the city that is called 
‘The perfection of lovelineness, 
The joy of all the earth’?”
2.17:
ע,𐤏 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has done what He planned,
He has filled His word
Which He commanded in days of old.
He has torn down, without compassion,
And He has let your enemy rejoice over you.
He has exalted the horn of your adversaries.
2.18:
צ,𐤑 Their heart cried out to Aḏonai,
“O wall of the daughter of Tsiyon,
Let tears run down like a river day and night.
Give yourself no respite,
Let your eyes have no rest.
2.19:
ק,𐤒 “Arise, cry out in the night,
At the beginning of the watches,
Pour out your heart like water
Before the face of Aḏonai. 
Lift your hands toward Him
For the life of your young children,
Who languish from hunger
At the head of every street.
2.20:
ר,𐤓 “See, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and look attentively
To whom have You done thus.
Should the women eat their offspring,
Infants of a tophaḥ?
Should the kohĕn and naḇi be slain 
In the Miqdash of Aḏonai?
2.21:
ש,𐤔 “Young and old lie on the ground in the streets.
My maidens and my young men have fallen by the sword.
You have slain them in the day of Your displeasure,
You have slaughtered without compassion.
2.22:
ת,𐤕 “Would You proclaim, as in a day of appointed time, 
The fears that surround me? 
And no one escaped or survived 
In the day of the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. 
Those whom I have nursed and brought up, 
My enemy has destroyed.”

3.1:
א,𐤀 I am the man who has seen affliction 
By the rod of His wrath.
3.2:
He has led me and made me walk 
In darkness and not light.
3.3:
Indeed, He has turned back, 
He has turned His hand against me all the day.
3.4:
ב,𐤁 He has worn out my flesh and my skin, 
He has broken my bones.
3.5:
He has piled up against me, 
And surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
3.6:
He has made me dwell in dark places 
Like the dead of old.
3.7:
ג,𐤂 He has hedged me in, and I do not go out, 
He has made my chain heavy.
3.8:
Also, when I cry and shout, 
He shuts out my prayer.
3.9:
He has blocked my ways with hewn stone, 
He has made my paths crooked.
3.10:
ד,𐤃 He is to me like a bear lying in wait, 
A lion in hiding.
3.11:
He has turned aside my ways
And torn me in pieces,
He has laid me waste.
3.12:
He has bent His bow
And stood me up as a target for the arrow.
3.13: ה,𐤄 He made the arrows of His quiver pierce my kidneys.
3.14:
I have been a mockery to all my people,
Their song all the day.
3.15:
He has filled me with bitterness,
He drenched me with wormwood.
3.16:
ו,𐤅 And He has broken my teeth with gravel,
He has covered me with ashes.
3.17:
And You have removed my being far from peace, 
I have forgotten goodness.
3.18:
And I said, “My strength and my expectancy 
Have perished from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
3.19:
ז,𐤆 Remember my affliction and my anguish, 
The wormwood and the gall.
3.20:
Your being indeed remembers 
And bows down upon me.
3.21: This I recall to my mind, therefore I wait:
3.22:
ח,𐤇 The kindnesses of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! 
For we have not been consumed,
For His compassions have not ended.
3.23:
They are new every morning,
Great is Your trustworthiness.
3.24:
“𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is my Portion,” says my being,
“Therefore I wait for Him!”
3.25:
ט,𐤈 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is good to those waiting for Him, 
To the being who seeks Him.
3.26:
It is good - both to wait and to be silent, 
For the deliverance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.27: It is good for a man to bear a yoke in his youth.
3.28:
י,𐤉 Let him sit alone and be silent, 
Because He has laid it on him.
3.29:
Let him put his mouth in the dust, 
There might yet be expectancy.
3.30:
Let him give his cheek
To the one who smites him -
He is filled with reproach.
3.31: כ,𐤊 For Aḏonai does not cast off forever.
3.32:
For though He afflicted,
Yet He shall show compassion
According to the greatness of His kindnesses.
3.33:
For He has not afflicted from His heart, 
Nor does He grieve the children of men.
3.34:
ל,𐤋 To crush under His feet 
All the prisoners of the earth,
3.35:
To turn aside the right-ruling of man 
Before the face of the Most High,
3.36:
Or pervert a man in his cause - 
This Aḏonai does not approve.
3.37:
מ,𐤌 Who was it that spoke,
And it came to be!
Has Aḏonai not commanded it?
3.38:
Do not the evils and the good
Come out of the mouth of the Most High?
3.39:
What? Should mankind complain,
A living man, because of his sins?
3.40:
נ,𐤍 Let us search and examine our ways, 
And turn back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
3.41:
Let us lift our hearts and hands 
To Ĕl in the shamayim:
3.42:
We, we have transgressed and rebelled. 
You, You have not forgiven.
3.43:
ס,𐤎 You have wrapped Yourself
With displeasure and pursued us.
You have slain,
You have not shown compassion.
3.44:
You have wrapped Yourself 
With a cloud, so that prayer does not pass through.
3.45:
You make us as scum and refuse
In the midst of the peoples.
3.46: פ,𐤐 All our enemies have opened their mouth against us.
3.47:
Fear and a snare have come upon us,
Shame and ruin.
3.48:
Streams of water run down my eyes
For the ruin of the daughter of my people.
3.49:
ע,𐤏 My eyes flow out and do not cease, 
Without stopping,
3.50: Until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks down and sees from the shamayim.
3.51:
My eyes pain my being
Because of all the daughters of my city.
3.52:
צ,𐤑 My enemies hunted me down 
Like a bird, without cause.
3.53:
They have cut off my life in the pit, 
And they threw stones at me.
3.54:
Waters flowed over my head; 
I said, “I am cut off!”
3.55:
ק,𐤒 I called on Your Name,
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the lowest pit.
3.56:
You have heard my voice,
Do not hide Your ear from my groaning,
From my outcry!
3.57:
You drew near on the day I called on You; 
You said, “Do not fear!”
3.58:
ר,𐤓 O Aḏonai, You pleaded the case for my being; 
You have redeemed my life.
3.59:
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You have seen my oppression; 
Judge my case.
3.60:
You have seen all their vengeance, 
All their plans against me.
3.61:
ש,𐤔 You have heard their reproach, 
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, all their plans against me,
3.62:
The lips of those rising against me, 
And their scheming against me all the day.
3.63:
Look at their sitting down and their rising up; 
I am their song.
3.64:
ת,𐤕 Repay them, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
According to the work of their hands.
3.65:
Give them a veiled heart, 
Your curse upon them!
3.66:
Pursue and destroy them in displeasure, 
From under the shamayim of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.

4.1:
א,𐤀 How dim the gold has become,
The fine gold changed!
The stone of the Miqdash
Are scattered at the head of every street.
4.2:
ב,𐤁 The precious sons of Tsiyon
Who were weighed against fine gold,
How they have been reckoned as clay pots,
The work of the hands of the potter!
4.3:
ג,𐤂 Even jackals have presented their breasts,
They have nursed their young.
The daughter of my people has become as cruel,
As ostriches in the wilderness.
4.4:
ד,𐤃 The tongue of the infant has clung
To the roof of its mouth for thirst;
Children asked for bread,
No one breaks it for them.
4.5:
ה,𐤄 Those who ate delicacies
Have been laid waste in the streets;
Those who were brought up in scarlet
Have embraced dunghills.
4.6:
ו,𐤅 And the wickedness of the daughter of my people
Is greater than the sin of Seḏom,
Which was overthrown in a moment,
And no hands were wrung over her!
4.7:
ז,𐤆 Her Nazirites were brighter than snow
And whiter than milk;
More ruddy in body than rubies,
Their cut like sapphire.
4.9:
ט,𐤈 Better off were those pierced by the sword
Than those pierced by hunger;
For these pine away,
Pierced through for lack of the fruits of the field.
4.10:
י,𐤉 The hands of the compassionate women
Have boiled their own children;
They became food for them
In the destruction of the daughter of my people.
4.11:
כ,𐤊 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has completed His wrath,
He has poured out His burning displeasure.
And He kindled a fire in Tsiyon,
And it consumed her foundations.
4.12:
ל,𐤋 The melaḵim of the earth did not believe, 
Nor any of the inhabitants of the world,
That an adversary and enemy
Would enter the gates of Yerushalayim.
4.13:
מ,𐤌 It was because of the sins of her neḇi’im,
The wickednesses of her kohenim,
Who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
4.15:
ס,𐤎 They shouted at them, 
“Away! Unclean! Away! Away! Touch not! 
”When they fled and staggered, 
They said among the gentiles, 
“They shall stay no longer.”
4.16:
פ,𐤐 The face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 scattered them.
He no longer regards them.
They showed no respect for the kohenim
Nor favor to the elders.
4.17:
ע,𐤏 While we exist, our eyes are consumed,
Watching vainly for our help.
In our watchtower we watched for a nation
That could not save.
4.18:
צ,𐤑 They have hunted our steps
From going in our streets.
Our end was near,
Our days were completed,
For our end had come.
4.19:
ק,𐤒 Our pursuers were swifter
Than the eagles of the shamayim.
They came hotly after us on the mountains
And lay in way for us in the wilderness.
4.20:
ר,𐤓 The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
Was caught in their pits,
In whose shadow we had thought
To live among the gentiles.
4.21:
ש,𐤔 Rejoice and be glad,
O daughter of Eḏom,
You who dwell in the land of Uts!
The cup is to pass over to you too,
So that you become drunk and make yourself naked.
4.22:
ת,𐤕 Your wickedness has been completed,
O daughter of Tsiyon.
He no longer prolongs your exile.
He shall punish your wickedness,
O daughter of Eḏom,
He shall uncover your sins!

5.1:
Remember, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, what has come upon us.
Look, and see our reproach!
5.2:
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers,
And our houses to foreigners.
5.3:
We have become orphans, fatherless,
Our mothers are like widows.
5.4:
We had to pay for our drinking water,
And our wood comes at a price.
5.5:
We have been pursued close onto our neck,
We have labored and had no rest.
5.6:
To Mitsrayim we have given a hand;
To Ashshur, to be satisfied with bread.
5.7:
Our fathers sinned, they are no more.
We have borne their wickednesses.
5.8:
Servants have ruled over us;
There is no one to deliver from their hand.
5.9:
With our lives we bring in our bread,
Because of the sword of the wilderness.
5.10:
Our skin as become as hot as an oven,
Because of the burning heat of scarcity of food.
5.11:
They have humbled the women in Tsiyon,
The maidens of the cities of Yahuḏah.
5.12:
Rulers were hung up by their hands,
And elders were not respected.
5.13:
They have taken young men to grind,
And youths stumbled under wood.
5.14:
Elders have ceased from the gate,
Young men from their song.
5.15:
The joy of our heart has ceased,
Our dancing has turned into mourning.
5.16:
The crown has fallen from our head.
Woe to us, for we have sinned!
5.17:
Because of this our heart has been sick,
Because of these our eyes have become dim,
5.18:
Because of Mount Tsiyon which is laid waste;
Foxes have gone roaming in it.
5.19:
You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, remain forever,
Your throne from generation to generation.
5.20:
Why do You forget us forever,
Forsake us for length of days?
5.21:
Turn us back to You, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 
And let us turn back, 
Renew our days as of old.
5.22:
For have You completely rejected us?
You have been wroth with us, exceedingly!
